items.title: Public Meetings to Consider Zoning Amendments
Barbara Lee, on behalf of the Elora Arts Council, introduced Terry Copp.
notes: Terry and his late wife, artist Linda Copp, have been residents of Wellington County for more than 50 years. Terry spoke about Linda's love of Elora and Wellington County and her work as an artist using the batik technique. He explained that batik is a traditional Indonesian art form in which the artist works from light to dark, applying wax to preserve the lightest areas as layers of colour are added. Following the completion of the batik process, the entire artwork is covered in wax.

items.title: Heritage Permit - 490 Tower Street South, Fergus
notes: Report from Deanna Maiden, Senior Development Planner
Deanna Maiden, Senior Development Planner provided a report recommending approval of the designated property 490 Tower Street South, Fergus.

She noted the owner has applied to demolish the accessory shed located at the rear of the property, due to its condition, the property also contains a one-and-a half storey single-detached limestone farmhouse, built in 1882. In accordance with the Township’s Heritage Permit By-law, approval from Council is required to demolish or remove a designated building or structure on the property.

Tyler Sager, Managing Director of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk responded to questions and provided clarification on the difference between matters included on the consent agenda and those requiring separate consideration through reports.

items.title: Naturalized Gardens and Vegetation Maintenance
notes: Report from Satnam Chauhan, Supervisor of Bylaw and Licensing Satnam Chauhan, Supervisor of Bylaw and Licensing provided a report recommending amendments the Township’s Clean Yards By-law. These proposed changes would recognize and permit naturalized gardens under defined maintenance standards, improve clarity and enforceability of the by-law, and would assist with the overlapping yard maintenance provisions from the Property Standards By-law.

He noted the proposed amendments are intended to preserve the Township’s ability to address unmanaged and safety nuisance concerns at a property. It would also assist with vegetation definitions by distinguishing intentional and maintained naturalized landscaping from neglected property conditions.

S. Chauhan responded to comments and questions from Council about the percentage of By-law complaints relating to neglected property conditions, the Clean Yards By-law relating to vacant building lots, public notice of changes and overall enforcement of the By-law and the complaints process.

items.title: Municipal Alcohol Policy
notes: Report from Kristen Bettiol, Manager of Community Development Kristen Bettiol, Manager of Community Development gave a presentation providing a brief overview of the proposed Municipal Alcohol Policy and highlights. The new policy establishes a clearer and more comprehensive framework for the safe service and consumption of alcohol on Township property and is intended to support responsible community use of Township facilities while strengthening public safety, improving administrative consistency, and reducing municipal risk.

K. Bettiol responded to comments and questions from Council regarding consultation with community groups, the event application process, reducing municipal risk and liability, and overall fees and costs.

items.title: Confederation Park Restricted Donation Agreement
notes: Report from Adam Gilmore, Managing Director of Community Services Adam Gilmore, Managing Director of Community Services provided a brief report outlining the agreement that has been negotiated with the Donor to assist in funding planned improvements to Confederation Park.

He noted that the donor is interested in advancing improvements that were originally planned for later phases of the project. Specifically, the end-to-end accessible pathway, scheduled for construction later this year, the design of the new lookout deck, would be recognized as the Don Watson Trail and Lookout in honour of Don Watson, who served the Town of Fergus for 42 years before retiring as Public Works Superintendent.
A. Gilmore responded to comments and questions from Council regarding community engagement, invasive species removal and park lighting.

items.title: 2026 Fees and Charges By-law Amendment
notes: Report from Adam McNabb, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer Adam McNabb, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer presented a report recommending an amendment to Schedule “B” of the Fees and Charges By-law which would include an introduction of a new Annual Retainer Fee for Technical Rescue Services through the new Technical Rescue Services Agreements.

items.title: Asset Management - 2026 Update Report
notes: Report from Adam McNabb, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer Adam McNabb, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer provided an update on the 2025 Asset Management Plan, endorsed by Council in June 2025.

He provided an overview of the progress, asset conditions, financial update, the levels of service, other areas of focus for 2026/2027, the overall asset management strategy, financing strategy and doubling of funding of the Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund (OCIF).

A. McNabb responded to comments and questions from Council regarding designation of vehicles, recreational equipment, other sources of funding, target levels of service, modelling future levels of service, assessment of condition and life cycle management.
A. Gilmore responded to questions from Council regarding bike lanes.

items.title: Water and Wastewater Public Corporation Model
notes: Report from Dan Wilson, CAO

Dan Wilson, CAO provided a report related to the establishment of a new model for water and wastewater service delivery through municipal service corporations, the Province of Ontario is advancing a legislative and regulatory framework to enable the creation of Water and Wastewater Public Corporations.

He indicated the model is not framed as a voluntary tool for municipalities and that the province has established a list of municipalities who will be required to deliver water and wastewater services through the publicly owned Water and Wastewater Corporation.

D. Wilson responded to comments and questions from Council regarding water wastewater billing, debt and funding, AMO’s involvement, Provincial intent, timelines, staff time and expression of potential interest.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receive report FIN2026-15; and THAT Council direct staff to communicate the support resolution to the Acting Minister of Infrastructure and MPP Joseph Racinsky; and WHEREAS recent municipal infrastructure funding programs by the Government of Canada and Province of Ontario have tended to prioritize growth-related or housing-enabling infrastructure projects over infrastructure renewal needs; AND WHEREAS the Government of Ontario has regulated municipal infrastructure asset management through O. Reg 588/17 (Asset Management Planning for Municipal Infrastructure) under the Infrastructure for Jobs and Prosperity Act, 2015; AND WHEREAS municipal asset management plans and the Financial Accountability Office of Ontario have identified that municipalities have significant state-of-good-repair backlogs and renewal needs for infrastructure; AND WHEREAS the Government of Ontario doubled the Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund (OCIF) from $200M/year to $400M/year for 2021-2026 but has not publicly committed to maintaining this level of funding beyond 2026; AND WHEREAS the OCIF has become a vital and indispensable resource for municipalities, assisting them with improving their asset management programs and meeting community preserving infrastructure renewal needs; AND WHEREAS increased geopolitical uncertainty is threatening the economic prosperity of Canada, Ontario, and every municipality; AND WHEREAS municipal infrastructure is a key enabler and preserver of economic prosperity; AND WHEREAS the Municipal Finance Officers’ Association of Ontario (MFOA) has heard from its members and their municipalities concerns regarding the potential erosion of existing municipal infrastructure and thus service levels in light of the ongoing focus on housing enabling infrastructure by grant funding programs; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that The Township of Centre Wellington supports MFOA’s letter to the Ministry of Infrastructure requesting that the doubling of the Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund be made permanent in advance of the allocations for the 2027 calendar year, helping municipalities to continue building housing- enabling infrastructure while preserving the economic value provided by existing infrastructure.
